items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.eaAreaName: East Anglia
items.message: Flooding is possible throughout today, Sunday 22nd November. This is due to tide locking, where high tides restrict normal drainage of the river out to sea. We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak compared to published tide tables. We are closely monitoring the situation. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 10am on Monday 23rd November, or as the situation changes.

items.description: Clanfield Brook for Clanfield Village and the Shill Brook for Bampton
items.eaAreaName: Thames
items.message:
High river levels may lead to flooding. 

Flooding of low lying land and roads is possible today, 22/11/2026, in the Clanfield area. The next 24 hours is expected to be mostly dry. We expect river levels to remain high throughout the day. 

We are monitoring the situation. Avoid using low lying footpaths and any bridges near local watercourses. 

This message will be updated by 10:00 23 Nov 2026 or as the situation changes.

items.eaAreaName: Solent and South Downs
items.message: River levels are high but slowly falling in the Eastern Yar. Residual flooding impacts to Golf Links Road and Moreton Common Road may still be occurring. Ditches around Fort Holiday Park will struggle to drain while river levels are high. Sunday 22/11/2026 and Monday 23/11/2026 are mostly dry. However, more rain is forecast Tuesday 24/11/2026 and Wednesday 25/11/2026. If heavy rain affects the Eastern Yar, flood risk will increase again. We are  monitoring rainfall and river levels and will ensure the river is kept free of reported blockages. Take care and avoid walking‚ cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 13:00 23/11/2026.

items.description: South Devon coast at Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
High tides, strong winds and large waves are expected to cause flooding tomorrow. 
Flooding is expected 3 hours either side of high tides 
Areas at risk include exposed coastal areas at Hallsands, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton, Blackpool Sands, Teignmouth Promenade and Dawlish. The high tide at Teignmouth on Sunday morning is at 04:15. Forecast total high tide level is 2.14mAOD, which is 0.56 metres above tide table level. Strong force 6 South Easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2.1m are forecast over the high tide. High tide on Sunday evening is at 16:30. Forecast total high tide level is 2.15mAOD, which is 0.4 metres above tide table level. Strong force 6 Easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2m. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 2:00PM on Sunday 22 November or as the situation changes.
